open_points.subject: Flow composition persistence (State 0 action vs A05 rule 7)
open_points.text: State 0: "compose and prove a flow ... the version is kept either way"; A05 rule 7: "Composition refuses, before anything is kept, a flow version whose node ids repeat ... the proof never sees such a version."
open_points.question: When composition input is structurally invalid (duplicate node ids/port names, file carriage on flow I/O, missing/extra class fields), must the kernel still keep a FlowVersion record or refuse without keeping anything?
options: Keep the version record and return an unproven proof result.
Refuse composition and keep nothing for these structural faults.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse composition and keep nothing for the structural faults listed in A05 rule 7.

open_points.subject: Trial-case admission checks ordering (A04 rule 1)
open_points.text: A04 rule 1: "Either way it is added only when its input values fit the contract version's input ports, its expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports, and every value is within stored_value_bytes_max and every file within trial_fixture_bytes_max — the first failing condition in this order is named."
open_points.question: Inside "fit the ... ports", what deterministic order is used to choose the named failure when multiple ports fail (missing port, extra port, schema mismatch, wrong carriage, size, etc.)?
options: Define a strict per-port/per-check order (for example, port name order, then presence, then schema/carriage).
Return one generic "does not fit ports" refusal without naming a specific port/check.
open_points.default_guess: Validate ports in port-name order and report the first concrete mismatch.

open_points.subject: Mapped-node element selection criterion in one pass (A13 rule 2)
open_points.text: A13 rule 2: "A mapped node, once selected, runs in list order every element that has no concluded record and can run ... before the next node is selected."
open_points.question: What exact predicate defines "can run" for a mapped element at that moment, and is readiness re-evaluated between elements in the same mapped-node pass or only once at pass start?
options: Re-evaluate readiness before each element and run all currently runnable unconcluded elements in index order.
Snapshot runnable elements at pass start and run only that snapshot this pass.
open_points.default_guess: Re-evaluate per element and run runnable unconcluded elements in ascending index order.

open_points.subject: HTTP response Content-Type absence/ambiguity for file outputs (A09 rule 3)
open_points.text: A09 rule 3: "A binding with a file output ... the body is that file, whose Content-Type ... must equal the port's media type; otherwise ..."
open_points.question: If the response for a file output has no Content-Type header, or multiple conflicting Content-Type headers, how is it classified?
options: Treat as output-not-fitting rule 3 -> NodeExecution contract_violation (and attempt applied for non-read).
Treat as transport/protocol failure -> service_unreachable/outcome_unknown/operation_failed depending on method/class.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as output-not-fitting rule 3, i.e., contract_violation.

open_points.subject: Run-start input validation failure precedence within each port (A12 rule 1)
open_points.text: A12 rule 1: "each value, in port name order, fits its port's schema ... and is within stored_value_bytes_max"
open_points.question: If a single input port value both violates schema and exceeds size, which refusal reason must be reported?
options: Schema failure has precedence, size checked only after schema passes.
Size failure has precedence, schema checked only for values within size.
